answer: Simultaneous cross-examination checks catch farms that share one operator. Paired seats must each answer, within 10 seconds, a question about their own signed work history on a copper assay run, a ridge path survey, or a canyon drainage map. One controller juggling N personas cannot keep N distinct live contexts; a miss or cross-leak of another seat's private detail flags the whole set. So N fakes demand N concurrent memory spaces and N response threads, a cost that scales linearly and cannot be pooled onto one model session.
